Here is a detailed description of every file created for the Tic Tac Toe JavaScript game. ## Project folder ```text /workspace/projects/tic-tac-toe-js ``` This folder contains the full game. It is a simple browser-based project using only HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No external libraries or build tools are required. --- ## 1. `index.html` ```text /workspace/projects/tic-tac-toe-js/index.html ``` ### Purpose This is the main HTML file for the game. It defines the page structure and connects the CSS and JavaScript files. When you open this file in a browser, it loads the Tic Tac Toe interface. ### What it contains The file includes: - The document setup - A title for the browser tab - A link to the stylesheet - The visible game interface - A script link to the JavaScript logic ### Main sections #### HTML document setup ```html ``` This tells the browser that the file is an HTML5 document and that the language is English. #### Metadata ```html ``` These lines ensure: - Text characters display correctly - The page scales properly on mobile devices #### Page title ```html Tic Tac Toe ``` This sets the browser tab title. #### CSS link ```html ``` This connects the page to `styles.css`, which controls how the game looks. --- ### Game layout The visible part of the game is inside: ```html
``` This wraps the full game and helps center it on the page. Inside it is: ```html
``` This acts as the main card/container for the game. --- ### Header text ```html

Simple JavaScript Game

Tic Tac Toe

``` These show the small label and the main game title. --- ### Scoreboard ```html
``` The scoreboard has three sections: - Player X score - Draw count - Player O score Each score has its own element: ```html 0 0 0 ``` These IDs are important because `script.js` uses them to update the scores while the game runs. --- ### Status message ```html

Player X's turn

``` This displays whose turn it is or the result of the round. Examples: ```text Player X's turn Player O's turn Player X wins! It's a draw! ``` The `aria-live="polite"` attribute helps screen readers announce changes in the game status. --- ### Game board ```html
``` This contains the 9 clickable cells of the Tic Tac Toe board. Each cell is a button: ```html ``` There are 9 buttons total, with `data-index` values from `0` to `8`. The indexes represent the board positions: ```text 0 | 1 | 2 --------- 3 | 4 | 5 --------- 6 | 7 | 8 ``` The JavaScript uses these indexes to know which square was clicked. --- ### Control buttons ```html ``` These buttons allow the player to: - Start a new round without resetting scores - Reset all scores and start over The JavaScript file uses the IDs `newRoundButton` and `resetButton` to attach click behavior. --- ### JavaScript link ```html ``` This loads the game logic from `script.js`. It is placed near the end of the body so the HTML elements exist before the script tries to access them. --- ## 2. `styles.css` ```text /workspace/projects/tic-tac-toe-js/styles.css ``` ### Purpose This file controls the visual design of the game. It handles: - Background colors - Card layout - Board layout - Cell styling - Button styling - Responsive behavior - Hover and focus effects - Winning square highlighting --- ### CSS variables At the top, the file defines reusable color variables: ```css :root { --bg: #111827; --card: #1f2937; --cell: #374151; --cell-hover: #4b5563; --text: #f9fafb; --muted: #cbd5e1; --accent: #38bdf8; --accent-2: #f472b6; --win: #22c55e; } ``` These make it easier to update the theme. For example: - `--accent` is used for Player X - `--accent-2` is used for Player O - `--win` is used for the winning line highlight --- ### Page setup ```css body { margin: 0; min-height: 100vh; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; color: var(--text); background: radial-gradient(circle at top, #1e3a8a 0, var(--bg) 45%); } ``` This creates the dark blue page background and sets the default font. --- ### Game centering ```css .game-wrapper { min-height: 100vh; display: grid; place-items: center; padding: 24px; } ``` This centers the game card both vertically and horizontally. --- ### Game card ```css .game-card { width: min(94vw, 480px); padding: 28px; border-radius: 24px; background: rgba(31, 41, 55, 0.92); box-shadow: 0 24px 80px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35); text-align: center; } ``` This creates the rounded card that contains the game. It has: - A maximum width of 480px - Padding - Rounded corners - A dark semi-transparent background - A shadow for depth --- ### Scoreboard styling ```css .scoreboard { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 10px; margin-bottom: 18px; } ``` The scoreboard is displayed as a three-column grid. Each score box has its own small background: ```css .scoreboard div { padding: 12px 8px; border-radius: 14px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07); } ``` --- ### Status message styling ```css .status { min-height: 28px; margin: 0 0 18px; color: var(--muted); font-size: 1.1rem; font-weight: 700; } ``` This styles the message that tells whose turn it is or who won. --- ### Board layout ```css .board { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 12px; margin: 0 auto 22px; } ``` This creates the 3-by-3 Tic Tac Toe grid. --- ### Cell styling ```css .cell { aspect-ratio: 1; border: 0; border-radius: 18px; color: var(--text); background: var(--cell); font-size: clamp(2.6rem, 15vw, 5rem); font-weight: 900; cursor: pointer; } ``` Each cell is a square button. Important details: - `aspect-ratio: 1` keeps each cell square - `font-size: clamp(...)` makes X and O resize nicely across screen sizes - `cursor: pointer` shows the cell is clickable --- ### Hover and focus effects ```css .cell:hover:not(:disabled), .cell:focus-visible:not(:disabled) { background: var(--cell-hover); transform: translateY(-2px); outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.5); } ``` This makes cells respond visually when hovered or focused. The `:not(:disabled)` part prevents hover effects after a cell has already been played. --- ### Player mark colors ```css .cell.x { color: var(--accent); } .cell.o { color: var(--accent-2); } ``` Player X and Player O have different colors: - X is blue - O is pink --- ### Winning cell highlight ```css .cell.win { background: rgba(34, 197, 94, 0.28); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--win); } ``` When a player wins, the three winning cells get a green highlight. --- ### Control buttons ```css .controls { display: flex; gap: 12px; justify-content: center; flex-wrap: wrap; } ``` This lays out the New Round and Reset Score buttons. The primary button is blue: ```css .primary-button { color: #082f49; background: var(--accent); } ``` The secondary button is darker: ```css .secondary-button { color: var(--text); background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12); } ``` --- ### Mobile styling ```css @media (max-width: 420px) { .game-card { padding: 20px; } .board { gap: 9px; } .cell { border-radius: 14px; } } ``` This improves the layout on smaller screens by reducing spacing and rounding. --- ## 3. `script.js` ```text /workspace/projects/tic-tac-toe-js/script.js ``` ### Purpose This file contains all the game logic. It controls: - Player turns - Cell clicking - Placing X and O - Checking for wins - Checking for draws - Updating the status message - Updating the scoreboard - Starting a new round - Resetting the score --- ### Selecting HTML elements At the top, the script finds elements from the page: ```javascript const cells = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.cell')); const statusText = document.getElementById('status'); const newRoundButton = document.getElementById('newRoundButton'); const resetButton = document.getElementById('resetButton'); const xScoreText = document.getElementById('xScore'); const oScoreText = document.getElementById('oScore'); const drawScoreText = document.getElementById('drawScore'); ``` These variables allow JavaScript to update the page. For example: - `cells` is the list of the 9 board buttons - `statusText` is the turn/result message - `xScoreText`, `oScoreText`, and `drawScoreText` are the scoreboard values --- ### Winning combinations ```javascript const winningLines = [ [0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8], [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8], [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6], ]; ``` These are all possible winning lines in Tic Tac Toe. They represent: #### Rows ```text [0, 1, 2] [3, 4, 5] [6, 7, 8] ``` #### Columns ```text [0, 3, 6] [1, 4, 7] [2, 5, 8] ``` #### Diagonals ```text [0, 4, 8] [2, 4, 6] ``` --- ### Game state variables ```javascript let board = Array(9).fill(''); let currentPlayer = 'X'; let gameActive = true; let scores = { X: 0, O: 0, draws: 0, }; ``` These variables track the current state of the game. #### `board` Stores what is currently in each square. At the start: ```javascript ['', '', '', '', '', '', '', '', ''] ``` After some moves, it might look like: ```javascript ['X', 'O', '', '', 'X', '', '', '', 'O'] ``` #### `currentPlayer` Tracks whose turn it is. It starts as: ```javascript 'X' ``` #### `gameActive` Controls whether players can still click cells. It becomes `false` after a win or draw. #### `scores` Stores the scoreboard values. --- ### `handleCellClick(event)` ```javascript function handleCellClick(event) { ``` This function runs whenever a player clicks a cell. It does several things: 1. Gets the clicked cell 2. Gets the cell index 3. Checks if the move is allowed 4. Places the current player's mark 5. Checks if the current player won 6. Checks if the game is a draw 7. Switches to the other player Important guard check: ```javascript if (!gameActive || board[index] !== '') { return; } ``` This prevents moves if: - The game is already over - The clicked cell is already taken --- ### `placeMark(index)` ```javascript function placeMark(index) { board[index] = currentPlayer; cells[index].textContent = currentPlayer; cells[index].classList.add(currentPlayer.toLowerCase()); cells[index].disabled = true; } ``` This places the current player's mark into the selected cell. It updates both: - The internal JavaScript board - The visible HTML cell It also disables the clicked cell so it cannot be clicked again. --- ### `getWinningLine()` ```javascript function getWinningLine() { return winningLines.find((line) => { const [a, b, c] = line; return board[a] && board[a] === board[b] && board[a] === board[c]; }); } ``` This checks whether the current board contains a winning line. It returns the winning line if one exists. Example return value: ```javascript [0, 4, 8] ``` If there is no winner, it returns `undefined`. --- ### `endGameWithWinner(winningLine)` ```javascript function endGameWithWinner(winningLine) { ``` This function runs when a player wins. It does the following: 1. Stops the game 2. Adds 1 point to the winner's score 3. Updates the scoreboard 4. Shows the winner message 5. Highlights the winning cells 6. Disables all cells Example status message: ```text Player X wins! ``` The winning cells are highlighted using this class: ```javascript cells[index].classList.add('win') ``` That class is styled in `styles.css`. --- ### `endGameWithDraw()` ```javascript function endGameWithDraw() { ``` This function runs when all cells are filled and nobody wins. It: 1. Stops the game 2. Adds 1 to the draw score 3. Updates the scoreboard 4. Displays the draw message Example message: ```text It's a draw! ``` --- ### `switchPlayer()` ```javascript function switchPlayer() { currentPlayer = currentPlayer === 'X' ? 'O' : 'X'; statusText.textContent = `Player ${currentPlayer}'s turn`; } ``` This changes the active player. If the current player is X, it changes to O. If the current player is O, it changes to X. --- ### `startNewRound()` ```javascript function startNewRound() { ``` This resets the board but keeps the current scores. It: - Clears the board array - Sets the current player back to X - Makes the game active again - Resets the status text - Clears the visible cells - Re-enables all cells - Removes X, O, and win styling from the cells This is used by the `New Round` button. --- ### `resetScore()` ```javascript function resetScore() { ``` This resets the full game. It: 1. Sets all scores back to 0 2. Updates the scoreboard 3. Starts a new round This is used by the `Reset Score` button. --- ### `updateScoreboard()` ```javascript function updateScoreboard() { xScoreText.textContent = scores.X; oScoreText.textContent = scores.O; drawScoreText.textContent = scores.draws; } ``` This updates the visible scoreboard with the current score values. --- ### Event listeners At the bottom of the file: ```javascript cells.forEach((cell) => cell.addEventListener('click', handleCellClick)); newRoundButton.addEventListener('click', startNewRound); resetButton.addEventListener('click', resetScore); ``` These lines connect user actions to JavaScript functions. They make the game interactive. - Clicking a cell runs `handleCellClick` - Clicking New Round runs `startNewRound` - Clicking Reset Score runs `resetScore` --- ## 4. `README.md` ```text /workspace/projects/tic-tac-toe-js/README.md ``` ### Purpose This file explains what the project is and how to run it. It is useful if someone opens the project folder and wants a quick overview. --- ### Contents The README includes: ```markdown # Tic Tac Toe JavaScript Game ``` This is the project title. --- ### Description ```markdown A simple two-player Tic Tac Toe game built with plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. ``` This explains that the project does not use any frameworks or libraries. --- ### Feature list The README lists the game features: - Two-player local gameplay - Win and draw detection - Highlighted winning line - Score tracking for X, O, and draws - New round and reset score buttons - Responsive design for mobile and desktop --- ### Run instructions The README says you can open: ```text index.html ``` directly in a browser. It also gives an optional local server command: ```bash python3 -m http.server 8000 ``` If you run that command inside the project folder, you can visit: ```text http://localhost:8000 ``` --- ## Summary The game is made of four files: | File | Purpose | |---|---| | `index.html` | Creates the page structure and game board | | `styles.css` | Controls the visual design and responsive layout | | `script.js` | Contains all Tic Tac Toe game logic | | `README.md` | Explains the project and how to run it | Together, these files create a complete playable Tic Tac Toe game in the browser.
